untertitel: A first look at the *pretérito perfeito simples* (*comprei, comi, fui, tive, fiz*) – build sentences, ask questions, play memory. The full rule is an A2 topic.
grammatik: Pretérito perfeito simples: first look (eu forms)

grammatik.regel: First look: the *pretérito perfeito simples* talks about finished times: *ontem, ontem à noite, no sábado, na segunda-feira*. The full rule is an A2 topic; here you only meet the *eu* forms of a few common verbs. Regular: -ar verbs end in *-ei* (comprar → _comprei_), -er / -ir verbs in *-i* (comer → _comi_). Very common irregular verbs: ir → _fui_, fazer → _fiz_, ter → _tive_, vir → _vim_. Question to one person: *O que fizeste no sábado?* A bracketed word like (eu) says who is speaking; you don't write it.

redemittel.p1: O que _fizeste_ no fim de semana?

redemittel.p2: Muito bem! Agora diz uma frase.

soGehts: Cut pages 2 and 3 in half. Cut out the word cards on page 4 too.
On your own (page 2): Put the tiles in order and write four sentences in the *perfeito*. Change the blue verb to the *eu* form.
In pairs (page 3): Ask: “O que fizeste …?” Your partner answers with their sentence. Write the answer.
Game (page 4): Play memory with the word cards.
Finally: O que fizeste no fim de semana? Tell your partner.

hinweise: Blue tile = infinitive. Change it to the *eu* form of the past: cozinhar → cozinhei, ir → fui.
The time (no sábado, ontem à noite) comes first in these sentences.
Questions: O que fizeste …? A tile in brackets, like (eu) or (tu), says who: don't write it.

regeln: Cut out the 24 word cards and put them face down on the table.
A turns over two cards and reads them aloud.
Do they match (cozinhar – cozinhei)? Then A says a sentence: “Ontem cozinhei massa.”
The sentence is right? A keeps the pair and plays again. No pair, or the sentence is wrong: turn the cards back, and now it is B's turn.
Who has the most pairs at the end?
